item.title: I’ll work closely with Kwankwaso if elected, Obi reassures
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has reiterated willingness to work closely with his vice-presidential candidate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, to move the country forward. Obi gave the assurance on Thursday during a town hall meeting in Enugu, where he engaged supporters and stakeholders on the country’s challenges and his vision for national development. The former Anambra State governor said they would work together to tackle insecurity and restore safety across Nigeria if elected president in 2027. He said that securing lives and property would be a priority of his administration, promising to confront the security challenges threatening communities and livelihoods across the country. The presidential candidate regretted that the current administration had failed to protect the lives and property of Nigerians, which he maintained was the primary responsibility. Obi assured voters in the South East to vote for him because of his competence and ability to tackle challenges facing the nation. He challenged other presidential candidates to meet and discuss their plans, and warned the people not to be deceived by rhetoric and propaganda. On education, Obi said he would declare a state of emergency on education to enable his administration to tackle the issue of out-of-school children head-on, hinting that Nigerian children deserved quality education. In his remarks, the vice-presidential candidate of NDC, Kwankwaso, advised that nobody should be deceived by ethnicity, saying, “It’s obvious that Nigerians are going through numerous difficulties”. Kwankwaso lamented that people were facing challenges like insecurity, unemployment, poverty, hunger and so many other challenges. He explained that the only solution to achieve a new Nigeria was unity, diligence, perseverance and willingness. He urged Nigerians to come out en masse to cast, protect and follow up on their votes until results were announced, noting that it was not a one-man show but a collective responsibility. Also, Sen Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly, described Obi and his running mate, Kwankwaso, as the “best presidential ticket” to lead Nigeria. Umeh expressed confidence that the South-East would rally behind Obi in the 2027 presidential election, urging the people to remain resolute and resist attempts to intimidate or discourage them from pursuing their political choice. He also commended the resilience of supporters who, according to him, ensured that the meeting held despite reported attempts to frustrate the gathering. The senator further praised Kwankwaso for his efforts to build support in Northern Nigeria, expressing optimism that the Obi-led ticket could attract votes across the country. Umeh urged the people of the South-East to use their votes to make a strong political statement in 2027, declaring his support for Obi’s presidential ambition and calling on the region to unite behind the project. item.title: Inter, AC Milan unveil new stadium plans to replace San Siro
item.description: Inter and AC Milan unveiled their new “Generali Stadium” Thursday, which will replace the iconic San Siro stadium from the 2031/32 season. It will be shaped “low in the body, and it rises up at either end” behind the goals, architect Norman Foster said during a press conference in Milan. The design aims to bring spectators as close to the pitch as possible, with the stands behind the goals set at a steep 37-degree incline, said David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project. “The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling,” he said. “It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling, and everything that we needed to do here was to carry it into the (new) building”. Manica said the design team “started with proximity”. “We brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass,” he said. They also paid great attention to acoustics: the roof covers the stands, leaving only the pitch exposed, and is designed to “amplify the roar” of the fans, Manica said. “This building is steeper than many other new buildings are built today, and that’s intentional, because it allows us to bring those seats up and over the field as much as possible, and create that sense of intimacy and atmosphere,” he said. The stadium, sponsored by the Italian insurance giant Generali, will also be capable of hosting American football games, rugby matches and concerts. “I want the crowd to come to the new stadium and to feel that excitement that they felt before, and to feel the building, living and breathing with them as it does currently,” Manica said. AC Milan and Inter paid 197 million euros ($219 million) to acquire the current stadium and its adjacent parking areas, where they intend to build their new, shared home. The project for the new San Siro — which will have a capacity of 71,500 seats, compared to the current 75,000 — will cost the two clubs 1.2 billion euros. Construction is set to begin in 2028. Foster and Manica previously worked together on London’s Wembley Stadium. Milan’s current stadium — one of the most iconic in European football and often likened to a “concrete cathedral” — is the largest in Italy. But the venue, which opened in 1926, no longer meets the needs of spectators or the clubs, despite undergoing several renovations over the decades. San Siro, also known as the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, will be largely demolished once construction work on the new stadium nears completion. item.title: 2027: INEC grants provisional clearance to Pantami, Gwarzo – Source
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi & Ben Ngwakwe There were strong indications on Thursday night that the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC might have provisionally cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The clearance of both men is subject to the outcome of pending court cases, it was learned on Thursday night. In Gombe, Pantami’s supporters took over some major areas celebrating the development on Thursday night. INEC officials did not immediately react to Vanguard’s questions regarding the development. But a source said the decisions were reached at the commission’s meeting on Thursday to consider complaints from political parties and candidates whose names were left out of the lists published ahead of the 2027 elections. The source added that the commission had no objection to their candidacies, but that the pending legal proceedings could still affect the final outcome. The development comes after INEC dropped Pantami’s name from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State, although he appeared on the provisional list published on August 29. Pantami emerged as the PDP candidate after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. One of the aspirants for the ticket, Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, challenged his victory in court. A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again. His biggest hurdle was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time. Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had previously said that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027. The commission, however, rejected a petition by the PDP governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, who had asked it to review his exclusion from the list of candidates. item.title: ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star Patrick Stewart dies at 86
item.description: Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died at the age of 86, an official statement said Thursday. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement said. The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company before crossing the Atlantic to enjoy an acclaimed career on the US stage and screen. His best known Hollywood roles were as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and Professor Charles Xavier in multiple “X-Men” and related Marvel films. “His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement said. “He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.” AFP The post ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star Patrick Stewart dies at 86 appeared first on Vanguard News .

This is as the Theatre Commander of OPHK, Major General Ibikunle Ajose on Thursday commissioned the newly constructed three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu’s one year in office, which also reflects his commitment to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness. In a press statement signed by the Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni on Thursday said: “Troops of OPHK continued to record operational successes through sustained intelligence-led offensive operations aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and dismantling their networks across the theatre. “In a further operation, OPHK air assets, at about 9:20 pm on 28 October 2026, conducted an armed reconnaissance and air interdiction mission in the Kerenoa Marte Local Government Area of Borno State, resulting in the neutralisation of 15 terrorists and the destruction of an IED hideout. “The mission followed intelligence reports on terrorist activities in the area. item.title: Just In: Tinubu lands in Saudi Arabia for Umrah
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Thursday evening arrived in Saudi Arabia, landing at the King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah. He was received by Nigeria’s ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and the Saudi head of royal protocol Ahmad bin Thafir. The President is scheduled to perform Umrah, also known as the lesser hajj, and is expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the religious exercise. Thursday’s trip marks the second time Tinubu has travelled to Makkah to perform Umrah since assuming office on May 29, 2023. President Tinubu visited the holy city in November 2023, shortly after attending the Saudi-African Summit in Riyadh, where he also prayed for divine guidance in leading Nigeria. item.description: Former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win Imo State in the 2027 presidential election if he is on the ballot as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District. Okorocha is locked in a legal battle with his successor, Governor Hope Uzodimma, over the APC ticket for Imo West, with both laying claim to victory in the party’s primary election. ﻿ The APC, however, submitted Uzodimma’s name to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as its candidate, prompting Okorocha to challenge the decision in court. On Thursday, the Federal Capital Territory High Court ruled that Okorocha secured the majority of votes cast in the primary and should be declared the winner. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today hours after the judgment, Okorocha said his presence on the ballot would guarantee Tinubu’s victory in the state. “What is important to me now is how Asiwaju will be elected in Imo State. With this, my name coming on the ballot paper now, Asiwaju can be sure that his victory is given in Imo State,” he said. The former governor celebrated the ruling, insisting that the judiciary was not for sale. He also said Uzodimma had “met his Waterloo,” alleging that the court had pronounced that his documents “were forged”. Okorocha urged people in the South-East to approach the 2027 presidential election strategically, advising the Igbo to put political calculations ahead of emotions. item.title: Germany’s Zverev becomes tennis world No. 1
item.description: Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on Thursday as he beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open. The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week’s updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital. Long seen as tennis’ nearly-man, Zverev has enjoyed a stellar 2026, breaking his major duck by picking up the titles at the French and US Opens. Now he has broken further ground by becoming only the 30th man to claim top spot since the rankings were first published in 1973. He will be aged 29 years and 196 days when Monday’s new rankings are published, making him the second-oldest first-time number one after Australian John Newcombe. Due to a knee injury Italy’s Sinner decided to end his season at the start of October, opening the way for Zverev to dethrone him. And the big-serving Hamburg native ensured he did just that ahead of the season-ending ATP Finals next month by seeing off Martin Landaluce and Griekspoor in his opening two matches in Vienna. Zverev needed to save four match points against Spain’s Landaluce in his first-round match on Tuesday, but was much more comfortable as he defeated Griekspoor in straight sets to write his name into the history books. He raced out of the blocks on Thursday, breaking the 30-year-old Dutchman in the very first game and then confidently serving his way into a one-set lead. The second frame went to 5-5 before Zverev pounced on Griekspoor’s serve to get his nose in front. The match met an unexpected stoppage as Zverev brought up match point when a smash off the German’s racquet caused part of the electronic board behind Griekspoor to malfunction. But once the umpire covered the problematic panel up with a towel, Zverev then sealed his new ranking with an unreturnable serve. I have discountenanced their letter.” Similarly, Ajidagba confirmed receiving the invitation on Thursday afternoon, saying it was delivered at about 2:30 p.m. with instructions to report at the DSS office by 4:30 p.m. He, however, questioned the timing of the invitation, arguing that matters relating to the succession process were already before the courts. “I received the DSS invitation on Thursday at about 2:30 p.m., and I was told to report at their office by 4:30 p.m. There was, however, no way I could honour such an invitation when all of these matters are already in court. The status quo must be allowed to remain; that is the position of the law,” he said. There was no immediate confirmation from the DSS on the reported invitations or the allegations prompting them. The latest development comes against the backdrop of previous engagements between security agencies and stakeholders in the Awujale succession process. Security agencies, including the Ogun State Police Command, had reportedly summoned nine kingmakers in Ijebu-Ode and the three Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders on two occasions to appear at the police headquarters in Eleweran, Abeokuta. The invitations were said to be connected with allegations of bribery and financial inducement in the selection of a new Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland. Owoyemi has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in connection with the succession process. The three ruling house leaders have also instituted legal proceedings against the Ogun State government over the suspension of the selection process, which has remained stalled since January 2026. In August, the Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders approached the Ogun State High Court sitting in Ijebu-Ode, seeking orders compelling the completion of the process for selecting the next Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland. The suit, numbered HCJ/149/2026 and dated August 21, 2026, was instituted by Owoyemi, Ajidagba and Yusuf. The defendants include Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Mr Oluwasina Ogungbade (SAN); the Ogun State Executive Council; the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Ganiyu Hamzat; and the Secretary of Ijebu-Ode Local Government. Also joined as defendants are members of the Awujale Afobaje/Kingmakers Council, including Olorogun Sonny Kuku, Chief Rasheed Adesanya, Chief Oluwaranti Lekan Osifeso, Chief Jimi Lawal, Chief Abimbola Okenla, Chief Kunle Ogunade, Chief Agboola Alausa, Chief Adebisi Adaran and Chief Ayotunde Ola Odulaja. Among other reliefs, the claimants are asking the court to determine whether the state government had the legal authority to order or facilitate the alleged entry into and locking of the Awujale palace on January 20, 2026. According to the claimants, the action was intended to physically prevent the kingmakers from convening and concluding the statutory process for selecting a successor to the late monarch. The dispute has further complicated efforts to fill the vacant traditional stool, with the government maintaining that the process must be conducted peacefully and in accordance with the applicable procedures. Meanwhile, Governor Abiodun has assured the people of Ijebuland that a new Awujale will emerge before May 29, 2027. The governor gave the assurance on Tuesday at the Ogun East Senatorial District stakeholders’ meeting in Ijebu-Ode, where he engaged representatives of various interest groups on traditional affairs, governance and the economic prospects of the district. According to a statement issued on Wednesday, Abiodun reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to ensuring a smooth and acceptable succession process. “On the succession process for the revered Awujale stool, Abiodun assured the people that his administration was committed to facilitating a smooth, peaceful and widely acceptable process leading to the emergence of a new monarch,” the statement said. The governor acknowledged the significance of the Awujale institution to the cultural heritage, identity and unity of Ijebuland, urging residents to remain calm and patient while the necessary procedures were being concluded. He added that his administration was giving the matter the attention it deserved to ensure that the process was completed peacefully and that the eventual emergence of a new monarch enjoyed the acceptance and support of the people. The Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025 following the death of Oba Adetona, who ruled for 65 years and was widely regarded as one of Nigeria’s longest-reigning traditional rulers. The Ogun State Government halted the succession process in January 2026, citing petitions from security agencies and other stakeholders. The suspension followed an earlier halt in December 2025 over procedural concerns. A total of 95 aspirants—94 princes and one princess—reportedly emerged from the Fusengbuwa ruling house nomination exercise held in Ijebu-Ode in December 2025 before the government suspended further proceedings. item.description: By Efosa Taiwo Stablecoins could transform cross-border payments by reducing transaction delays, improving liquidity and making money transfers faster and more accessible, speakers at Moonshot 2026 have said. The speakers made the remarks during a panel session titled “The New Payment Backbone: Stablecoins as Core Infrastructure for Global Liquidity” on the Emerging Tech Stage, where industry leaders discussed how stablecoins could reshape payments across Africa and the global financial system. Mercy Emmanuel, Stablecoin & Blockchain Vertical Lead, Flutterwave, said stablecoins could simplify international transfers, which often involve multiple intermediaries and take several days to complete. “Sending money from Lagos to Nairobi goes through a lot. It could take two to five days before it gets to its destination. Stablecoins collapse all these,” Emmanuel said. She likened the technology to a moving train that operates without the restrictions of banking hours and time zones, arguing that it could make payments almost instantaneous and allow businesses to conduct transactions seamlessly alongside their online operations. According to her, stablecoins could also encourage businesses to rethink their payment processes and build more efficient financial operations. “Stablecoins are here to optimise the financial system, not displace the traditional way,” she said, adding that the financial industry was moving towards a system in which the focus would be on how quickly and efficiently money could move from one point to another. item.title: Grealish dropped for Everton’s League Cup tie after disciplinary breach
item.description: Jack Grealish was dropped for Everton’s League Cup fourth round clash against Newcastle on Thursday after “a breach of club discipline”. It was reported that the breach related to Grealish’s unauthorised absence from training. The 31-year-old missed Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Arsenal in the Premier League due to an illness. Grealish, who is on a second season-long loan from Manchester City, had started Everton’s three Premier League matches prior to their defeat against champions Arsenal. The 31-year-old has made six appearances for David Moyes’s side this term, most recently in their loss against Chelsea on October 17. Grealish has been dogged by criticism of his off-pitch behaviour for several years amid reports of nightclub incidents that saw him fall out of favour at City. After playing a key role in City’s treble-winning campaign in 2022-23, Grealish became an increasingly sidelined figure at the Etihad Stadium. Everton are facing Newcastle for a place in the League Cup quarter-finals, with Fleetwood awaiting the winner after their shock victory over Arsenal on Tuesday. item.title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Africa must move from content creation to value capture’ — Tech leader Juliet Ehimuan
item.description: By Efosa Taiwo Juliet Ehimuan, founder of Beyond Limits and former Director of Google West Africa, has urged African creatives and technology entrepreneurs to move beyond content creation to building sustainable businesses that own intellectual property and capture value from their work. Ehimuan made the call while speaking on artificial intelligence (AI) and the future of African creativity at Moonshot 2026 during a keynote speech on Thursday. She said Africa’s creative economy remained underdeveloped, stressing the need to turn the continent’s creative talent into commercially viable enterprises capable of generating greater economic value. “Our creative economy is still less than 2% of GDP,” she said, highlighting the need for a shift from producing content to building businesses around it. According to her, African creators must focus on owning the intellectual property behind their work and exploring different ways to commercialise it. “We need to move from content creation to value capture. We need to move from having creative talents to building enterprises. We should move from content creation to IP,” Ehimuan said. She explained that intellectual property ownership could open up multiple revenue streams, noting that a book could be adapted into a series, while a podcast could generate additional commercial opportunities. “There are so many ways to monetise content if you have the IP for that,” she said, emphasising the importance of owning intellectual property and the infrastructure needed to distribute and commercialise creative products. Ehimuan outlined three priorities for Africa’s creative and technology sectors: adopting and developing AI capabilities, building and owning valuable assets, and establishing businesses capable of reaching wider markets. On AI adoption, she encouraged African businesses to develop their capabilities and stay ahead of technological changes, noting that the technology could improve productivity and create new opportunities across industries. She also urged creators and businesses to protect their rights and permissions while developing distinctive intellectual property that could be commercialised over time. item.title: Photos: Tech, AI, creative economy dominate conversations on Day 2 of Moonshot 2026
item.description: Day two of Moonshot by TechCabal 2026 brought together technology leaders, startup founders, creatives, investors and industry professionals for conversations on the future of Africa’s digital economy, with sessions spanning artificial intelligence, financial technology, the creative economy and emerging technologies. The event featured multiple stages, including the Startup Stage, Emerging Tech Stage and Creative Economy Stage, where speakers explored the opportunities and challenges shaping Africa’s technology and business landscape. Discussions examined questions such as “Can African Players Build the Infrastructure Creators Need?” and “Who Do We Trust With the Future of Money?” , reflecting growing interest in the infrastructure, innovation and trust required to support the continent’s digital transformation. Beyond the stage discussions, the gathering provided opportunities for networking, knowledge-sharing and engagement among participants working across technology, media, finance and the creative industries. item.title: I bleached my skin to get movie roles — Nollywood actress Habibat Jinadu
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nollywood actress Habibat Jinadu has revealed that she bleached her skin to secure acting roles, saying dark-skinned and slim actresses struggle to get opportunities in the film industry. Jinadu made this known in an interview with BBC Yoruba, where she recounted how pressure to meet the industry’s preferred physical appearance influenced her decision to bleach her skin. “I bleached my skin because if you were dark-skinned, then you would not get a role. Also, if you were not chubby but slim, you would not get a role,” the actress said. Explaining how she responded to the situation, Jinadu said she decided to bleach her skin and wait for the acting opportunities she believed would follow. “So, I went ahead, bleached my skin and started expecting to get roles. And indeed, I started getting roles,” she said. However, the actress disclosed that the change in her complexion made it difficult for people to recognise her outside the screen, despite her growing acting opportunities. “But people could not recognise me any longer. If I stepped out to buy something, people would go like, ‘You look familiar,’ ‘You look like an actress,’ and all sorts,” she recounted. Jinadu said she was unhappy with the experience but continued bleaching her skin as she tried to establish herself in the industry. “I was not happy with it, but I kept on pushing,” she said. The actress also revealed that she began experiencing injuries and skin tears from minor bruises while working on movie sets. “Then, I started sustaining injuries and tears from minor bruises on sets and all,” she said. According to Jinadu, the reality of her situation became clearer in 2023 when she became pregnant and had to stop bleaching her skin. “It all dawned on me when I got pregnant in 2023. And when you are pregnant, you cannot bleach your skin,” she said. She explained that stopping the practice brought another challenge, as people began criticising her appearance after her complexion changed. “When I eventually stopped, people started abusing me and calling me all sorts of names,” she said. item.title: Police arrest two masquerades over alleged extortion, others in Akwa Ibom
item.description: Police in Akwa Ibom State have arrested two Ekpo masquerade participants over allegations of extorting money from residents and assaulting members of the public in Ikot Ekpene. The suspects were arrested at about 6pm on Monday, October 26, along the Ukana/Abak highway during an operational show of force, the police said. The state police spokesperson, Timfom John, identified the suspects in a statement on Thursday as Ine Isong, 29, of Ukana Ikot Esoh Village, and Emmanuel Ekpenyong, 20, from Ikono Local Government Area. John said the suspects were allegedly found in possession of Ekpo masquerade costumes and attire, machetes, spears and arrows. “Preliminary reports indicate that the suspects and other persons allegedly involved in the activities had been terrorising residents and extorting money from unsuspecting members of the public,” the statement said. It added that some people, particularly women, were allegedly assaulted during the activities. John said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged offences and identify other persons who might be involved. The Commissioner of Police, Baba Azare, warned that the command would not tolerate the use of cultural practices or masquerade activities as a cover for criminality, intimidation, extortion or violence. “While respecting lawful cultural traditions, the command remains resolute in ensuring that no individual or group takes the law into their own hands or threatens the peace and security of residents,” Azare said. item.title: Estêvão will ‘have his moment’ at Chelsea — Alonso
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso has promised Brazilian teenager Estêvão will get his opportunity this season, despite the winger’s limited playing time and omission from the Blues’ Carabao Cup quarter-final defeat to Liverpool. Alonso said he understood the 19-year-old’s frustration after he was an unused substitute in Wednesday’s penalty shootout loss, insisting it was his responsibility to manage the youngster’s development and involvement in the team. “I understand his situation and that he could be happier for sure,” Alonso said at his post-match press conference. “Every player wants to play, wants to be part of the team. We have had some intense games, and there will be moments for everything. “I’m sure Estêvão will have his moment. It’s my responsibility, and we need to deal with that.” Estêvão has played only 172 minutes across eight appearances for Chelsea this season, starting just twice under Alonso. His lack of opportunities attracted attention after he remained on the bench against Liverpool, despite Cole Palmer and João Pedro being unavailable for the cup tie. The Brazilian featured in two of Chelsea’s four matches since the latest international break, coming on as a substitute on both occasions. His reduced role follows a promising debut campaign in which he scored eight goals and provided three assists in 36 appearances before his season was cut short by injury. Estêvão also missed the 2026 World Cup because of a hamstring injury, adding to the challenges surrounding his recent progress. The teenager has yet to register a direct goal contribution in the 2026-27 campaign, although he has attempted seven shots, created six chances and completed five of his 14 dribbles, according to the supplied statistics. Alonso’s comments suggest the winger remains part of Chelsea’s plans despite his limited involvement so far. Chelsea will return to Premier League action on Saturday when they host Manchester United, offering Estêvão another opportunity to feature as the London club look to respond to their cup exit. item.title: Paris Gun Attack Leaves One Dead, Five Wounded As Suspect Faces Terrorism Probe
item.description: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week that killed one person and wounded five including a child has admitted to “targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African,” prosecutors said on Thursday. Earlier this week the 39-year-old man, identified as Kevin T., had said he did not “dispute the material facts”, but contested “the racist nature of his crimes”. On Thursday, national terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen told a news conference that Kevin T. now claims he chose the location for his actions because it was “a hotbed for Islamists”. The victims were shot from a vehicle driving through the towns of Trappes and La Verriere west of Paris. The suspect was detained later Friday with a machine gun and tear-gas grenades in his car. He has since been held in police custody and was set to appear before a judge later on Thursday, Christen said, noting that he had requested that he be held in pretrial detention. France’s counter-terrorism public prosecutor Olivier Christen speaks during a press conference at the Paris Judicial Court, in Paris on October 29, 2026, following the terrorist attack that took place on October 23 in Trappes and La Verriere.Photo by ANNE-CHRISTINE POUJOULAT / AFP Of the four people seriously injured in the attack, “three of the victims remain hospitalised as I speak, and one of them is still in life-threatening condition,” Christen said. He noted the “very high level of preparation” behind the attack. Kevin T. nevertheless denied any “terrorist intent,” viewing his actions as “legitimate,” the prosecutor said. The opening of a judicial investigation by the office of the national anti-terrorism prosecutor (PNAT) allows a judge to take charge of the case, specifically regarding charges of “murder and attempted murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise”. A search of the suspect’s home had uncovered “weapons or weapon components, specifically a magazine, two pairs of brass knuckles, a steel bayonet, and a silencer,” Christen said. Also found were several “books, including a Quran, a Bible, and Adolf Hitler’s Mein Kampf”, as well as stickers celebrating the far-right National Rally (RN) party. Christen said the stickers bore slogans such as “Long live France, RN, proud to be French”, but they were not produced by the party led by Marine Le Pen, who is leading opinion polls to succeed Emmanuel Macron as French president in elections next spring. Kevin T. had told investigators that “he designed the stickers found in his home himself, and then ordered them to be manufactured via Amazon more than a year ago.” The suspect had said that “he is neither a member of nor a sympathiser with any political party”, Christen said.
